-/// By default (and currently the only option) the terminal will not be

+/// The terminal is not connected to an external process (may change in the future). Input sent on
+/// the channel is processed by the terminal and echoed to `buf`. This is useful to display ANSI
+/// terminal sequences returned as part of an RPC message, or similar. [terminal-concepts]
 ///
-/// Note: |:ls| reports the buffer as "R" (running) until the channel is closed. |chanclose()|
+/// The terminal processes two byte streams in opposite directions:
 ///
-/// Note: To initialize the terminal size, display the buffer in a window first. E.g. for a floating display,
+/// 1. INTO the terminal: bytes a child process would write to its stdout (terminal escape
+///    sequences, text, etc.). Push these in via |nvim_chan_send()|. The terminal parses them and
+///    renders to `buf`.
+/// 2. OUT of the terminal: bytes the child would read from its stdin. Receive these via the
+///    `on_input` callback. Includes:
+///    - Keypresses in terminal mode (sent raw as they would be to the pty master end: CR is sent as

+/// local chan

comment_data.body:
@zeertzjq @janlazo this might be too aggressive, but I think it's the direction we should go for future Vim patches. There are probably a bunch of relevant patches from Vim 9.0/9.1 . But for Vim 9.2+ I think we should plan to reject most of their patches.

If you have major concerns we can adjust this in a followup.

+HOW TO DECIDE IF A VIM-PATCH IS WANTED
+
+Legacy Vim is becoming much less relevant to Nvim: we expect to decline the

+a "deny-list". Generally, only modules explicitly noted in the "OWNED BY VIM"

comment_data.body:
I dropped the "reasoning" sentence.

> When has Nvim redesigned buffer/window behavior?

Not a redesign yet, but floatwin and cmdwin are very different. And we should consider simplifying how buffer deletion is handled, since it's a source of endless bugs.

comment_data.body:
Unless the next release is 1.0, it's too early to take this stance because of the grey area between  "owned" and "unwanted" for the remaining patches even if the scope is restricted to v9.2+ or "new features/behavior" that are  contrary to Neovim's goals.

Focus on the updated criteria for what makes a patch "relevant" because tooling can demonstrate/explain this criteria.

----

Idea:

You've brought up moving code from vim-patch.sh to vimpatch.lua but ... we could go further by moving in `runtime/lua/` and moving the "low-level" details to that lua module so that `:h dev-vimpatch` can be "high-level" instead.
